'''Denzel Valentine''' (born November 16, 1993) is an American [[college basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]] and represent the United States for the [[United States men's national basketball team|USA Basketball Select Team]].<ref name="mlive.com">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2016/06/denzel_valentine_gary_harris_n.html|title=Denzel Valentine, Gary Harris named to USA Basketball select team|website=MLive.com|access-date=2016-06-07}}</ref><ref name=realgm>{{cite web|title=Denzel Valentine Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Denzel-Valentine/Summary/44077|website=''[[RealGM]]''|accessdate=27 March 2015}}</ref>

==High school career==
Valentine attended [[J. W. Sexton High School|J.W. Sexton School]], where he was coached by his father, [[Carlton Valentine]] (former Michigan State player),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://statenews.com/article/2016/03/denzel-valentine-and-carlton-valentine-have-legacy-with-michigan-state-basketball|title=Denzel Valentine comes from a lineage of Spartan Basketball|website=The State News|access-date=2016-03-12}}</ref> and played alongside future Michigan State teammate [[Bryn Forbes]] and Iowa basketball player [http://www.hawkeyesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/anthony_clemmons_786823.html Anthony Clemmons].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hawkeyesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/iowa-m-baskbl-mtt.html|title=Official Men's Basketball Roster - Hawkeye Sports Official Athletic Site|website=www.hawkeyesports.com|access-date=2016-03-13}}</ref>

=== Sophomore Year (2009-10) ===
As a sophomore Valentine averaged 10.9 points, 5.8 assists and 6.3 rebounds, leading [[J. W. Sexton High School|Sexton]] to state title game. He was awarded 2010 Class B honorable mention all-state.<ref name="msuspartans.com">{{Cite web|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/denzel_valentine_825018.html|title=Denzel Valentine Bio - Michigan State Official Athletic Site|website=www.msuspartans.com|access-date=2016-03-13}}</ref>

=== Junior Year (2010-11) ===
In 2011, Valentine earned First-Team All-State Class B selection as chosen by the [[Detroit Free Press]] and [[The Detroit News]] and [[Lansing State Journal]] honored him on their Dream Team. He led [[J. W. Sexton High School|Sexton High School]] to 2011 Class B State Championship, the school's first state title in 51 years, tallying 17 points, six rebounds and three assists in 75-60 win over [[Muskegon Heights High School|Muskegon Heights]] in the title game. His averages were 12.7 points, 7.9 rebounds, 8.5 assists, 5.4 steals and 1.1 blocks as a junior. In 2011 he attended the NBA Top 100 Camp.<ref name="msuspartans.com"/>

=== Senior Year (2011-12) ===
He averaged 14 points, 11 rebounds and nine assists per game as a senior, leading the Big Reds to a 27-1 record. Valentine was selected to be the [[Lansing State Journal]] Player of the Year and [[Associated Press]] Class B Player of the Year as a senior.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|title=Denzel Valentine Bio|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/denzel_valentine_825018.html|website=''MSUSpartans.com''|accessdate=27 March 2015}}</ref> Nearly averaged a triple-double as a senior with 14 points, 11 rebounds and nine assists, leading the Big Reds to a 27-1 record.

As a recruit, Valentine was ranked among the top-100 players in the nation by the following;
* [[Rivals.com]] (#81) (#15 shooting guard)
* [[ESPNU College Basketball|ESPNU100]] (#98) (#26 small forward)
* [[Scout.com]] (#27 small forward) <ref name="msuspartans.com"/>

==College career==

=== Freshman Year (2012-13) ===
As a Freshman, Valentine appeared in all 36 games, starting 15, averaging 20.8 minutes. He averaged 5.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, ranking fourth on the team, and 2.4 assists, ranking second on the squad. On six occasions, Valentine scored in double figures, including a season-high 14 points against [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] on Jan. 30 (MSU was 6-0 when he scored in double figures). His first career start was earned in the fourth game of the season, scoring 12 points against [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]] (11/20). Valentine's brother, [[Drew Valentine|Drew]], was a senior on the [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland Golden Grizzly]] squad that Valentine posted a double-double against, scoring 10 points and grabbing a season-high 10 rebounds, while dishing out a season-high six assists. He grabbed six or more rebounds in 11 contests, leading [[Michigan State University|MSU]] in rebounding in five contests. Other top rebound efforts included a team-high nine boards against [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] (2/12), and eight each against [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]] (11/9) and [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] (1/13). The eight boards against [[University of Connecticut|Connecticut]] were the fifth-most ever by an MSU freshman in his Spartan debut. Along with rebounding, Valentine showed the ability to distribute the ball. He led MSU in assists in 10 games, including a season-high six helpers against both [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland]] and [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] (3/23) in the third round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]], while posting four assists or more in nine contests. Following his successful freshman year, he was the recipient of MSU's Unsung Player Award (voted on by players).<ref name="msuspartans.com"/>

=== Sophomore Year (2013-14) ===
As a sophomore Valentine appeared in 38 games, starting 33, averaging 8.0 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 3.8 assists in 29.4 minutes per contest. He was the only Spartan to appear in all 38 games, ranking second on the team with 33 starts, and third in minutes per game (29.4 mpg). Valentine's season finished strong as he started the final 30 games of the season. He ranked second on the squad in assists (3.8 apg), third in rebounds (6.0 rpg) and fifth in scoring (8.0 ppg), and was the only player in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] to rank in the Top 15 in both rebounding (t-11th) and assists (8th). In conference games, he ranked seventh in the Big Ten in rebounding (6.4 rpg) and sixth in assists (4.1 apg), while being ranked third overall in the Big Ten in assist-to-turnover ratio (2.1) and second in conference games (2.3). Valentine's ability to rebound improved as he was ranked seventh in the Big Ten in defensive rebounding overall (4.8 drpg) and tied for fourth in conference games (5.0 drpg). He led MSU in rebounding in 11 games and in assists in 16 games, including four games doing both. Valentine put his skills on display by recording three double-doubles, including in games against [[New Orleans University|New Orleans]] (12/28; 10 points, 13 rebounds), [[Illinois Fighting Illini|Illinois]] (1/18; 15 points, 11 rebounds), and [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] (2/6; 11 points, 11 rebounds); finished just four assists short of a triple-double against [[New Orleans University|New Orleans]] and [[Penn State Nittany Lions|Penn State]] after recording six assists in both contests. His three point shooting increased and was ranked fourth on the team in 3-point field goals made (43) and third in attempts (114) Valentine ranked third on the team with 37 steals. His season-high for scoring was 16 points in games against [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] (2/13) and [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] (2/20), yet he scored in double-figures in 16 games. Furthermore, he recorded double-figure rebounds in five games, and grabbed six or more boards in 22 games. He dished out five or more assists in 11 games, including eight games with six or more, including a season-high nine assists against [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] (3/6), while recording seven against [[Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers|Mount St. Mary's]] (11/29). He tallied two or more steals in 10 games, including four each against [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland]] (12/14), [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] (1/11) and [[Penn State Nittany Lions|Penn State]] (2/6). Valentine's improvement from his freshman year was rewarded.<ref name="msuspartans.com"/>

=== Junior Year (2014-15) ===
With [[Adreian Payne]] and [[Gary Harris]] leaving [[Michigan State University|MSU]] for the [[2014 NBA draft|NBA Draft]], [[Keith Appling]] leaving due to graduation (eventually to the NBA), the dismissal of [[Kenny Kaminski]], and the transfer of [[Russell Byrd]], Valentine would see a mass increase in leadership and an expanded role on the team. Before the season started he was awarded one of the three captain spots. He was the only player in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] to rank in the top 15 in scoring (12th, 14.5 ppg), rebounding (11th, 6.3 rpg) and assists (7th, 4.3 apg). Valentine also ranked in the Top 15 in conference games in scoring (12th, 14,6 ppg), rebounding (t-7th, 6.6 rpg) and assists (7th, 4.1 apg). Valentine filled the stats for [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] and ranked second on the team in scoring, rebounding and assists. He was the only Spartan to start all 39 games. In the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]], he averaged 15.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 3.6 assists. History was made when Valentine became the 48th player in [[Michigan State University|MSU]] history to score 1,000 career points during his 18-point effort against [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] (3/27) in the NCAA Tournament Sweet 16. Valentine's three point shooting saw improvement as he ranked fifth in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] in 3-point field-goal percentage (.416), second in 3-point field goals made (2.6), third in the Big Ten in 3-point field goals made (2.6) in Big Ten games, and he turned in the third-best single-season total for made 3-pointers in [[Michigan State University|MSU]] history (102). Ranked eighth in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] in assist-to-turnover ratio overall (1.8) and 10th in Big Ten games (1.9). He led the Spartans with a .826 free-throw percentage, including .857 in the NCAA Tournament and scored in double figures in 29 contests, including eight games with 20 points or more Valentine led [[Michigan State University|MSU]] in scoring in 16 games, in assists in 19 contests and in rebounding seven times. Scored a season-high 27 points vs. Minnesota (2/26), including knocking down 7-of-12 3-pointers. His other top-scoring efforts include 25 points vs. [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] (11/28), knocking down six 3-pointers and 25 points vs. [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] (2/1), adding seven rebounds and seven assists against the [[Michigan Wolverines|Wolverines]]. In the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|Big Ten Tournament]] quarterfinals, Valentine posted 23 points against [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] (3/13) and in the [[Final four|Final Four]] he scored 22 points vs. [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (4/4). Valentine proved to be "Mr Versatility" by recording three [[Double (basketball)|double-double]]<nowiki/>s, ranking second on the team, including games against [[Santa Clara University|Santa Clara]] (11/24; 13 pts., 11 reb.), [[Nebraska Cornhuskers|Nebraska]] (1/24; 21 pts., 11 reb.) and [[Duke University|Duke]] in the [[Final four|Final Four]] (4/4; 22 pts., 11 reb.). He grabbed seven or more rebounds in 17 games, including eight games with eight or more boards and recorded a season-high 11 rebounds against both [[Santa Clara Broncos|Santa Clara]] (11/24) and [[Nebraska Cornhuskers|Nebraska]] (1/24) Assists came easy as he dished out six or more assists in 16 games, including eight contests with seven or more and recorded a season-high eight assists against [[Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions and Golden Lady Lions|Arkansas-Pine Bluff]] (12/6), [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]] (12/17) and [[Northwestern Wildcats|Northwestern]] (2/10). Valentine finished third on the team with 35 steals. To end a year of great success Valentine saw a busier award season. Perhaps one of Valentine's most memorable moments came on [[Valentine's Day]] 2015, he hit the game winning shot in a matchup versus [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] and finished with 17 points.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rodgers|first1=Joe|title=Michigan State's Denzel Valentine hits game winner on Valentine's Day|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2015-02-14/happy-valentines-day-michigan-state-game-winning-shot-ohio-state-spartans-denzel-valentine-vine-video-watch|accessdate=April 22, 2015|work=[[The Sporting News]]|date=February 14, 2015}}</ref>

=== Senior Year (2015-16) ===
Valentine's senior year at [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] is regarded as one of the best single seasons by a Spartan ever. Valentine ranked among the [[NCAA Division I|NCAA]] leaders when it came to [[Three-point field goal|3-point]] shooting his senior season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/143|title=Three-Point Field-Goal Percentage {{!}} DI Men's Basketball Statistics - NCAA.com|website=NCAA.com|access-date=2016-03-12}}</ref> He accumulated many awards and won Michigan State's first [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|College Basketball Player of the Year Award]] since [[Draymond Green]] won the [[NABC Player of the Year]] in 2012. Valentine shined during the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|Big Ten Tournament]] in [[Indianapolis]], earning tournament Most Outstanding Player while winning Michigan State's fifth championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031316aac.html|title=2016 Big Ten Men's Basketball All-Tournament Team Big Ten Conference Official Site|website=www.bigten.org|access-date=2016-03-14}}</ref> Valentine, along with Bryn Forbes, were selected to the NCAA College Basketball 3pt Contest following his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.collegeslam.com.prod.sportngin.com/participants?_ga=1.213032918.391393238.1459473513|title=PARTICIPANTS|website=College Slam|access-date=2016-04-01}}</ref> Valentine defeated his teammate in the first round of the competition when he rattled off 22 points compared to Forbes' 10. Valentine was eliminated from the competition in the semifinals when he hit 17 points, needing 23 to advance. Valentine's senior year also proved very effective in raising his draft stock. Valentine went from being potentially undrafted to being seen as a potential lottery pick in the 2016 NBA Draft.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2016/04/deyonta_davis_at_no_12_denzel.html|title=Deyonta Davis at No. 12, Denzel Valentine at No. 16 in latest ESPN mock draft|website=MLive.com|access-date=2016-04-08}}</ref>

On November 17, 2015, Valentine became the 4th player in Michigan State history to record a [[triple-double]]. He had 29 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists in Michigan State's 79-73 victory over the fourth-ranked [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Goodman: Denzel Valentine's triple-double earns a call from Magic|url = http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14159021/denzel-valentine-delivers-triple-double-michigan-state-gets-call-magic-johnson|website = ESPN.com|accessdate = 2015-11-19}}</ref> It was the first triple-double of the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112315aaa.html|title=Big Ten Men's Basketball Weekly Release: November 23: Ten conference teams to compete in neutral site tournaments this week|accessdate=November 24, 2015|date=November 23, 2015|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref> On December 21, it was announced that Valentine would be sidelined for 2–3 weeks after he underwent an arthroscopic knee surgery, he returned on January 10, 2016 after missing.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rexrode|first1=Joe|title=MSU's Valentine out 2-3 weeks after knee surgery|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2015/12/21/denzel-valentine-injury-michigan-state/77699492/|accessdate=December 21, 2015|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=December 21, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25444798/denzel-valentine-returns-gets-10-points-in-michigan-state-victory|title=Denzel Valentine returns, gets 10 points in Michigan State victory|website=CBSSports.com|access-date=2016-03-02}}</ref>

He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith Trophy]] on February 11.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|accessdate=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}}</ref> On February 29, he was named a semifinalist of the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25499838/buddy-hield-ben-simmons-valentine-and-acc-trio-headline-oscar-robertson-finalists|title=Buddy Hield, Ben Simmons, Valentine  headline Oscar Robertson finalists|website=CBSSports.com|access-date=2016-03-08}}</ref> Valentine was also a finalist for the [[John R. Wooden Award]], the [[Adolph Rupp Trophy]], [[Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year]], and the [[NABC Player of the Year]].

Valentine finished the 2015–16 regular season averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 7.5 assists as MSU finished in second place in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]].

On March 8, [[USA Today]] named Valentine National Player of the Year over [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]]'s [[Buddy Hield]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigten/2016/03/08/usa-today-sports-college-basketball-player-year-denzel-valentine-michigan-state/81458046/|title=USA TODAY Sports college basketball Player of the Year: Michigan State’s Denzel Valentine|website=Detroit Free Press|access-date=2016-03-08}}</ref> The Big Ten also announced that Valentine was the Big Ten's Player of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2016/03/07/denzel-valentine-big-ten/81449266/|title=Michigan State's Denzel Valentine named Big Ten player of year|website=Detroit Free Press|access-date=2016-03-08}}</ref> On March 9, Valentine was named to the [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|Sporting News]] All-American Team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/list/4697744-sporting-news-college-basketball-all-americans-2015-16|title=Sporting News college basketball All-Americans 2015-16|website=Sporting News|access-date=2016-03-10}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Valentine hired agent [[B. J. Armstrong|B.J. Armstrong]] of [[Wasserman Media Group]]. Armstrong is also the agent for fellow [[Michigan State Spartans|Spartan]], [[Draymond Green]]. Valentine will train in [[Lansing, Michigan|Lansing]], [[Michigan]] until his [[Michigan State University|Michigan State]] graduation on May 6, when he will begin training in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2016/story/_/id/15146159/denzel-valentine-signs-bj-armstrong-draymond-green-agent|title=Valentine signs with Draymond Green's agent|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2016-04-08}}</ref>

Valentine was invited to attend the [[NBA Draft Combine|2016 NBA Draft Combine]] along with teammate [[Deyonta Davis]]. A few weeks before the draft began, there were growing concerns about one of Valentine's knees.<ref>http://www.woelfelspressbox.com/blog-entry/15/valentine-not-fazed-by-knee-chatter</ref> Despite Valentine and his former coach [[Tom Izzo]] claiming that his knee concerns are relatively minor, his draft stock is considered to be plummeting from being a late lottery selection to being selected late in the first round due, in part, of those concerns. However, Valentine would still end up being one of 19 different invitees for the [[2016 NBA Draft]]'s Green Room, implying he is still a mid-to-late first round candidate after all. He'd also be one of five invitees to get invited a few days after the original listing was revealed.

== National team career ==
Valentine has represented the United States multiple times at the international level.

=== Pan American Games ===
Valentine was a member of the 2015 [[USA Basketball]] Men’s [[Pan American Games]] team that captured the bronze medal with a 3-2 record at [[2015 Pan American Games]] in [[Toronto]], [[Canada]]. He was named on June 29 one of 22 players selected to attend USA Basketball training for the 2015 U.S. Pan American Men’s Basketball Team.

=== Team USA Select ===
Valentine was announced as a member of [[USA Basketball|USA Basketball's 2016 Men's Select Team]]. The select team competes against [[USA Basketball|USA Basketball's Men's National Team]] in [[Las Vegas]] during its training camp in preparation for the [[2016 Olympics]] from July 18–21. Former [[Michigan State]] teammate, [[Gary Harris]], was also among the 25 select team players. Valentine was one of just five in that group who were yet to play in the [[NBA]], along with [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]]'s [[Malcolm Brogdon]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]]'s [[Kris Dunn]]. [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]'s [[Brandon Ingram]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]'s [[Brice Johnson]]. All are projected first-round picks in the NBA draft later this month. The rest of the team was made up of young NBA players.<ref name="mlive.com"/>

== Personal life ==
Valentine was born on November 16, 1993, the son of Carlton and Kathy Valentine. His older brother Drew played collegiate basketball for [[Oakland University]], and is now an assistant coach there.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/denzel_valentine_825018.html|title=Denzel Valentine Bio - Michigan State Official Athletic Site|website=www.msuspartans.com|access-date=2016-04-08}}</ref>

On April 7, 2016, Valentine and his [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State basketball]] coach, [[Tom Izzo]], were featured as guests on [[Dancing with the Stars (U.S. TV series)|Dancing With the Stars]] where they learned from [[Artem Chigvintsev]] and [[Edyta Śliwińska|Edyta Sliwinska]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2016/04/tom-izzo-dwts-denzel-valentine|title=Exclusive: Watch Tom Izzo, Denzel Valentine and A’ja Wilson learn new moves from DWTS dancers|website=For The Win|language=en-US|access-date=2016-04-08}}</ref>

On April 8, 2016, during ESPN's College Basketball Award Show, Valentine was chosen to select 2015-16's [[Vine]] of the Year. The options were "[[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] turns defense-to-offense with full-court halftime buzzer-beater", "[[Wayne Selden, Jr.|Wayne Selden]]'s Uncle Anthony goes nuts after dunk vs. [[Baylor University|Baylor]]", "[[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|UNC]] big man eats up victory", and "Stunned security guard misses [[Kris Jenkins (basketball)|Kris Jenkins]]' game winner". Valentine selection was "Uncle Anthony. I would have lost it if I saw that."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2016/4/8/11394846/denzel-valentine-award-show-vine-of-the-year-uncle-anthony-wayne-selden-kansas|title=Denzel Valentine decides college basketball's Vine of the Year|last=O'Donnell|first=Ricky|website=SBNation.com|access-date=2016-04-11}}</ref>

[[Draymond Green]], [[Michigan State]] alum and Valentine best friend, has been defended on multiple occasions by Valentine.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://collegespun.com/big-ten/michigan-state-big-ten/denzel-valentine-defends-draymond-green-this-is-basketball-not-tiddly-winks|title=Denzel Valentine Defends Draymond Green: "This Is Basketball, Not Tiddly Winks"|date=2016-05-24|website=College Spun|language=en-US|access-date=2016-06-07}}</ref> Valentine has also called Green his 'big brother' [http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/news/nba-draft-2016-denzel-valentine-draymond-green-michigan-state-spartans-phoenix-suns/1xktclc3lzc6z1j3cfzqnmqy94].
